Adding a digital driver's license to your iPhone may soon expand to a 15th U.S. state.

Apple currently lists 14 states that support the feature, along with Puerto Rico, but backend data suggests another state is about to join…

Many people have long hoped for a day when they wouldn't need to carry physical identification documents, such as driver's licenses and passports, and could simply present a digital ID directly through their iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future may still be quite distant, but Apple took its first step back in 2021, when the company announced plans to allow iPhone users to add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. To date, 14 states have adopted this feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend data discovered by MacRumors indicates that Oklahoma is about to join the list.

We previously provided a detailed walkthrough on how to add your driver's license or state ID to the iPhone Wallet app. As noted at the time, it's worth keeping in mind that the digital ID may not completely replace the physical version, so unfortunately we still recommend everyone continue to carry their physical ID.

That said, at eligible TSA checkpoints and when verifying your age with merchants, the digital version can still help protect your privacy. The ID only confirms that you meet the age requirement, without disclosing any personal information, such as your date of birth.
